title: Signature declares `alg: none` against a published public key set
rationale: Verification is never attempted here rather than attempted and passed. A signature made under `none`, under a symmetric algorithm whose key the operator publishes, or under an undersized RSA key is evidence of nothing, because anyone holding the published material can produce it; counting it would inflate the paper's headline cryptographic-binding number with endpoints that have no binding at all.
key_provenance: Nothing here is signed, which is the point: the protected header base64url-decodes to {"alg": "none", "kid": "agent-example-key-1", "jku": "https://agent.example.org/.well-known/jwks.json"} and the signature is deliberately the empty octet sequence. The key set served below is the same published P-256 public key as in `c03-c04-c15-conforming-signed-card-verifies`, so the key resolves and only the algorithm differs between the two fixtures.

spec.quote: An Unsecured JWS uses the "alg" value "none" and is formatted identically to other JWSs, but MUST use the empty octet sequence as its JWS Signature value.
spec.verification: UNVERIFIED verbatim. docs/spec-mapping.md gives C15's anchor as 'RFC 7518, BCP 195' with no reproduced sentence. What the fixture actually pins is that the instrument refuses to count a signature made under `none` as cryptographic evidence, which is a property of the algorithm rather than of any one clause.

spec.quote: If any of the listed steps fails, then the signature or MAC cannot be validated. ... the JWS MUST be considered invalid.
spec.verification: paraphrase of RFC 7515 5.2's failure clause, NOT confirmed verbatim. checks_signed.py cites `RFC 7515` without a sentence; confirm before publication.
